guide.description: sed 's/pattern/replacement/' rewrites matching text on every line. By default it only replaces the FIRST match per line — add a trailing g (global) to replace every match on the line instead, or i to match case-insensitively (they can combine as gi). sed can also act on whole lines by number instead of substituting text: 'Nd' deletes line N (or 'N,Md' deletes a range), and multiple edits can be chained in one call with repeated -e. Matching is otherwise case-sensitive, just like grep.

flags.desc: (inside the expression, not a real flag) replace every match per line, not just the first
(inside the expression) match case-insensitively — combine with g as gi
as the whole expression: delete line N, or the range N through M
give another expression — repeat -e to chain several edits in one sed call

exercises.title: sed's first-match default
exercises.task: Replace the first lowercase 's' on every line of access.log with 'S'.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: sed 's/from/to/' <file> replaces only the FIRST match per line
The letter to replace is a lowercase s, swapped for an uppercase S

criteria.label: Replace only the first s per line
